'''Torleif Erik Oskar Ericson''' (born November 2, 1930) is a Swedish [[Nuclear physics|nuclear theoretical physicist]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|last=Feshbach|first=Herman|year=1991|title=Torleif Ericson on his sixtieth birthday|url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/10506899108260750|journal=Nuclear Physics News|language=en|volume=1|issue=3|pages=6|doi=10.1080/10506899108260750|bibcode=1991NPNew...1....6F |issn=1061-9127|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref name=":5">{{Cite journal|last=Weisskopf|first=Victor F.|year=1990|title=Foreword to the Festschrift for Torleif Ericson|url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/037594749090529U|journal=Nuclear Physics A|language=en|volume=518|issue=1–2|pages=ix|doi=10.1016/0375-9474(90)90529-U|bibcode=1990NuPhA.518D...9W|url-access=subscription}}</ref> He is known for '[[Ericson fluctuations|Ericson fluctuations']]<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":7" /> and the '[[Ericson-Ericson Lorentz-Lorenz effect]]'.<ref name=":8" /> His research has nurtured the link between nuclear and [[particle physics]].

== Biography ==

=== Career ===
Ericson studied physics at [[Lund University]], from where he obtained his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]],<ref name=":6">{{Cite thesis |last=Ericson |first=Torleif |url=https://lubcat.lub.lu.se/cgi-bin/koha/opac-detail.pl?biblionumber=849193 |title=Some statistical properties of excited nuclei |publisher=Lund University |year=1958 |language=English}}</ref> under the supervision of [[Ben Roy Mottelson|Ben Mottelson]] at the [[Nordic Institute for Theoretical Physics]] (Nordita), in 1958.

Ericson held positions as a [[postdoctoral researcher]] and an instructor at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]]<ref name=":7">{{Cite journal|last=Ericson|first=Torleif|year=1960|title=The statistical model and nuclear level densities|url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/00018736000101239|journal=Advances in Physics|language=en|volume=9|issue=36|pages=425–511|doi=10.1080/00018736000101239|bibcode=1960AdPhy...9..425E|issn=0001-8732|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|last=Ericson|first=Torleif|date=1960-11-01|title=Fluctuations of Nuclear Cross Sections in the "Continuum" Region|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.5.430|journal=Physical Review Letters|language=en|volume=5|issue=9|pages=430–431|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.5.430|bibcode=1960PhRvL...5..430E|issn=0031-9007|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|date=16 March 1981|title=This week's citation classic|url=https://garfield.library.upenn.edu/classics1981/A1981LE36300001.pdf|access-date=2021-10-29|journal=Current Contents|issue=11}}</ref> and as Visiting scientist at [[UC Berkeley|Berkeley]]<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":0">{{Cite book|last=Krige|first=J.|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gQbgQrYlpIoC&pg=306|title=History of CERN, III|publisher=Elsevier|year=1996|isbn=978-0-08-053403-9|pages=306|language=en|chapter=Physics in the CERN Theory Division: CERN, the centre of Europe}}</ref> from 1959 to 1960.

Following he joined [[CERN]]’s Theory Division,<ref>{{Cite book |last=Krige |first=J. |title=History of CERN, III |publisher=Elsevier |year=1996 |isbn=978-0-08-053403-9 |pages=293 |language=en |chapter=Physics in the CERN Theory Division: moving to Geneva |chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gQbgQrYlpIoC&pg=293}}</ref> first as a fellow, and then as a staff member in 1962.<ref>{{Cite web |title=INSPIRE: Torleif Ericson's author profile |url=https://inspirehep.net/authors/1010649 |access-date=2021-10-25 |website=inspirehep.net}}</ref> He was recruited by the Director-General, [[Victor Weisskopf|V. F. Weisskopf]], as the theoretical interface between particle and nuclear physics.<ref name=":5" />

Sabbatical year 1969/70 at MIT.

Invited guest professor at [[University of Geneva|Geneva]], [[University of Lausanne|Lausanne]], [[University of Louvain|Louvain]], [[University of Tokyo|Tokyo]] and [[Uppsala University|Uppsala]].

[[Adjunct professor]] at Uppsala University from 1993 within the framework of CERN's collaboration with Member States.

Official retirement from CERN in 1995,<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1734476/ |title=CERN lays on birthday treat for the Ericsons |date=December 2010 |publisher=CERN Courier |pages=41}}</ref> but still [[emeritus]] (honorary member of the personnel).<ref>{{Cite web |title=People {{!}} Department of Theoretical Physics |url=https://theory.cern/people |access-date=2021-10-25 |website=theory.cern}}</ref>

=== Research contributions ===
Moving from MIT to Berkeley he wrote two papers<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":7" /> in which he predicted what later became known as '[[Ericson fluctuations]]' and today is considered a prime example of [[quantum chaos]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite book|last1=Casten|first1=Richard F.|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=zujUCgAAQBAJ&pg=PA197|title=Nuclear structure physics: Celebrating the career of Peter Von Brentano|last2=Jolie|first2=Jan|last3=Kneissl|first3=Ulrich|last4=Lieb|first4=Klaus-peter|publisher=World Scientific|year=2001|isbn=978-981-4490-82-5|pages=197|language=en|chapter=Generic and non-generic features of chaotic systems: billiards and nuclei}}</ref> Initially the idea was met with resistance. However, the prediction stimulated in a large number of [[nuclear reaction]] studies, as reviewed a few years later with Mayer-Kuckuk,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Ericson|first1=T|last2=Mayer-Kuckuk|first2=T|year=1966|title=Fluctuations in Nuclear Reactions|journal=Annual Review of Nuclear Science|language=en|volume=16|issue=1|pages=183–206|doi=10.1146/annurev.ns.16.120166.001151|pmid=5334731|bibcode=1966ARNPS..16..183E|issn=0066-4243|doi-access=free}}</ref> and Ericson continued to develop the consequences in depth in a series of articles.<ref name=":4">{{Cite journal |last1=Richter |first1=Achim |last2=Weise |first2=Wolfram |year=1990 |title=Preface and biographical note |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/037594749090528T |journal=Nuclear Physics A |language=en |volume=518 |issue=1–2 |pages=i–viii |doi=10.1016/0375-9474(90)90528-T|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

In 1963, Ericson, after an initiative by [[Amos de-Shalit|A. de-Shalit]] and V.F. Weisskopf, organised an international conference on high-energy physics and [[nuclear structure]].<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/285021|title=1963 International Conference on High-energy Physics and Nuclear Structure: CERN, Geneva, Switzerland 25 Feb - 1 Mar 1963|date=1963|publisher=CERN|editor-last=Ericson|editor-first=Torleif Eric Oskar|series=CERN Yellow Reports: Conference Proceedings|location=Geneva}}</ref> The meeting turned out to be of significant importance both for Ericson's own career and the development of this field, as a new branch of nuclear physics.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":4" /><ref>{{Cite book|last=Pascolini|first=Alessandro|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=2tBKDwAAQBAJ|title=PAN XIII: Particles and Nuclei - Proceedings of the XIII International Conference|publisher=World Scientific|year=1994|isbn=978-981-4550-75-8|pages=xv|language=en}}</ref> The conference series, later generally referred to as PANIC, was the start of the field interfacing nuclear and particle physics and has developed into a triennial event. The series is sponsored by the [[International Union of Pure and Applied Physics]] and has been going on since then.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Particles and Nuclei International Conference 2021|url=https://pos.sissa.it/380/|access-date=2021-10-29|website=pos.sissa.it}}</ref>

In the 1960's much information in this field came from [[exotic atom]]s. This was limited but precise information. In this context Ericson studied how nuclei and particles manifest dielectric constants and magnetic susceptibilities in external fields. Furthermore, Ericson, together with his wife [[Magda Ericson]], were among the first to focus on the interaction of pions with nuclei and to study a regime that was intermediate between the low energies of traditional nuclear physics and elementary particles of higher energies.<ref name=":8">{{Cite journal|last1=Ericson|first1=M|last2=Ericson|first2=T. E. O|date=1966-02-18|title=Optical properties of low-energy pions in nuclei|url=https://dx.doi.org/10.1016/0003-4916%2866%2990302-2|journal=Annals of Physics|language=en|volume=36|issue=3|pages=323–362|doi=10.1016/0003-4916(66)90302-2|bibcode=1966AnPhy..36..323E|issn=0003-4916|url-access=subscription}}</ref> In particular the Ericsons realized that the [[pion]] behavior in nuclei is changed and that this produces major effects. This became known as the '[[Ericson-Ericson Lorentz-Lorenz effect]]' and has later influenced other areas of [[Many-body problem|many-body physics]].<ref name=":4" />

His interest in the quantitatively limits of pion physics in nuclei produced some of the most accurate  and parameter-free descriptions of observables in the entire nuclear physics.<ref name=":4" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Ericson |first1=T E O |last2=Rosa-Clot |first2=M |year=1985 |title=D-State Admixture and Tensor Forces in Light Nuclei |journal=Annual Review of Nuclear and Particle Science |language=en |volume=35 |issue=1 |pages=271–294 |bibcode=1985ARNPS..35..271E |doi=10.1146/annurev.ns.35.120185.001415 |issn=0163-8998|doi-access=free }}</ref>

He took interest in many different areas of physics. Together with [[Jose Bernabeu|J. Bernabeu]] and [[Cecilia Jarlskog|C. Jarlskog]], he realized that [[neutral current]]s imply [[parity violation]]s, which are strongly enhanced in certain [[muonic atom]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bernabeu |first1=J. |last2=Ericson |first2=T.E.O. |last3=Jarlskog |first3=C. |year=1974 |title=Parity violations by neutral currents in muonic atoms |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0370269374902627 |journal=Physics Letters B |language=en |volume=50 |issue=4 |pages=467–471 |doi=10.1016/0370-2693(74)90262-7|bibcode=1974PhLB...50..467B |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Bernabeu |first=Jose |date=17 September 2010 |title=Electroweak interactions: Celebration in Honour of Magda and Torleif Ericson's 80th Birthday |url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1293658 |website=CERN Document Server |at=See lecture after 28 minutes and 48 seconds}}</ref> He also developed an accurate test of [[T-violation|''T''-violation]] in nuclei based on [[Ericson fluctuations|fluctuations]],<ref name=":2" /> as well as an accurate empirical bound for [[anti-gravity]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Ericson |first1=T. E. O |last2=Richter |first2=A |date=1990-02-15 |title=Empirical Limits to Antigravity |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1209/0295-5075/11/4/001 |journal=Europhysics Letters |volume=11 |issue=4 |pages=295–300 |doi=10.1209/0295-5075/11/4/001 |bibcode=1990EL.....11..295E |issn=0295-5075|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

The activity on the interface between nuclear and particle physics led to that CERN set up various scientific committees,<ref>{{Cite book|last=Krige|first=J.|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gQbgQrYlpIoC&pg=333|title=History of CERN, III|publisher=Elsevier|year=1996|isbn=978-0-08-053403-9|pages=333–334|language=en|chapter=The early interest in nuclear physics at CERN: CERN’s Nuclear Structure Committee (NSC) and other scientific committees}}</ref> in which Ericson was deeply involved.

=== Administrative activities ===
In his role as chairman of the Nuclear Structure Committee, Ericson proposed in 1964, to build an on-line isotope separator, which later has become known as [[On-Line Isotope Mass Separator|ISOLDE]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=ISOLDE {{!}} timeline.web.cern.ch|url=https://timeline.web.cern.ch/timeline-header/140|access-date=2021-11-03|website=timeline.web.cern.ch}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Krige|first=J.|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gQbgQrYlpIoC&pg=353|title=History of CERN, III|publisher=Elsevier|year=1996|isbn=978-0-08-053403-9|pages=353–358|language=en|chapter=The SC: ISOLDE and Nuclear Structure: The ISOLDE collaboration is formed}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Ericson |first=Torleif |url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1139423 |title=Memorandum to the members of the NPRC on proposal of an isotope separator "on line" for the SC |publisher=CERN |year=1964 |series=CERN-NSC-64-2 |location=Geneva}}</ref> CERN eventually established  its  [[High-energy nuclear physics|ultrarelativistic heavy-ion programme]]<ref>{{Cite web|date=2017-03-17|title=A 30-year adventure with heavy ions|url=https://cerncourier.com/a/a-30-year-adventure-with-heavy-ions/|access-date=2021-10-26|website=CERN Courier|language=en-GB}}</ref> that over the years has attracted a large number of experimental physicists to the laboratory.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Jacob|first=Maurice|year=1990|title=Getting to know nuclear physics|url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/037594749090530Y|journal=Nuclear Physics A|language=en|volume=518|issue=1–2|pages=xi–xv|doi=10.1016/0375-9474(90)90530-Y|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Krige|first=J.|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gQbgQrYlpIoC&pg=351|title=History of CERN, III|publisher=Elsevier|year=1996|isbn=978-0-08-053403-9|pages=351|language=en|chapter=The SC: ISOLDE and nuclear structure: the early ISOLDE}}</ref>

In addition to carry out his research, Ericson has taken on a series of managerial tasks. For several periods he filled the role as deputy leader for the CERN Theory Division, he chaired the CERN  Nuclear Structure Committee, served as a member of the CERN Physics III Committee, Swedish Program Committee for Physics and in the [[IUPAP]] body International Committee for High Intensity Accelerators (ICHIA).<ref name=":4" /> Furthermore, Ericson was associated editor in the journal [[Nuclear Physics A]], with responsibility for intermediate energy, from 1976 to 2000.<ref>{{Cite journal|year=1976|title=Editorial Board|url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0375947476905200|journal=Nuclear Physics A|language=en|volume=258|issue=1|pages=iii|doi=10.1016/0375-9474(76)90520-0|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|year=2000|title=Editorial board|journal=Nuclear Physics A|language=en|volume=663-664|pages=IFC|doi=10.1016/S0375-9474(00)80002-0|doi-access=}}</ref> Since 1991 he is one of the general editors of the series Cambridge Monographs on Particle Physics, Nuclear Physics and Cosmology.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Cambridge Monographs on Particle Physics, Nuclear Physics and Cosmology|url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/series/cambridge-monographs-on-particle-physics-nuclear-physics-and-cosmology/B97F87127417D226CE11FAC609F6A0ED|access-date=2021-11-01|website=Cambridge Core|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last1=Donoghue|first1=John F.|author1-link=John Francis Donoghue (physicist)|url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/product/identifier/9780511524370/type/book|title=Dynamics of the Standard Model|last2=Golowich|first2=Eugene|last3=Holstein|first3=Barry R.|date=1992-07-23|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=978-0-521-36288-7|edition=1|doi=10.1017/cbo9780511524370|s2cid=119579852 }}</ref> Ericson has also been editor for a large number of conference proceedings.

== Awards and honors ==

* 1976: [[:sv:Professors namn|Title of Professor]] (Swedish: Professors namn) awarded by the [[Government of Sweden]]<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal|last1=Richter|first1=Achim|last2=Weise|first2=Wolfram|year=1990|title=Preface [to the Festschrift for Torleif Ericson]|url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/037594749090528T|journal=Nuclear Physics A|language=en|volume=518|issue=1–2|pages=i–viii|doi=10.1016/0375-9474(90)90528-T|url-access=subscription}}</ref>
* 1990: Foreign member of the [[Finnish Society of Sciences and Letters]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Members – Finska Vetenskaps-Societeten|url=https://scientiarum.fi/eng/members/|access-date=2021-10-25|website=scientiarum.fi}}</ref> 
*1990: Honorary professor, Shanghai Advanced Research Institute, [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]]<ref name=":3" /> 
* 1993: Member of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Members of the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences: Torleif Ericson |url=https://www.kva.se/en/contact/torleif-ericson-2/ |access-date=2023-03-13 |website=Kungl. Vetenskapsakademien |language=en-GB}}</ref>
*1994: Member of the [[Royal Society of Sciences in Uppsala]]

== Private life ==
Ericson is married to the French physicist [[Magda Ericson]] since 1957. Together they have two adult children. The Ericsons reside in [[Geneva]], [[Switzerland]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Profs. Ericson Torleif and Magda (-Galula) |url=https://www.local.ch/en/d/geneve/1202/prof-ericson-torleif-et-magda-galula-l8_MwE0h13SOJVqlBqwwEg |access-date=2022-05-20 |website=www.local.ch |language=en}}</ref>
